## Design assumptions

- All VM-C sections have the same steel density, so the lightest satisfactory strut is the one with the smallest gross area \(A\).
- \(A_{\mathrm{eff}}=A\); local and distortional buckling reductions are not required.
- The given effective lengths already include the end conditions:
  \[
  L_{ex}=L_{ey}=L_{ez}=3000\ \mathrm{mm}.
  \]
- Twist-restrained, free-to-warp ends are treated as torsionally pinned/fork-ended, giving the usual \(\pi^2EI_w/L_{ez}^2\) warping term.
- The load is concentric at the gross centroid, so there is no primary bending moment. The centroid–shear-centre offset is nevertheless included in the stability eigenvalue.
- Because \(x\)-\(x\) is the symmetry axis, strong-axis flexure is uncoupled. Weak-axis flexure and torsion are coupled through \(x_0\).
- Self-weight is neglected because it was not specified.

## Elastic buckling equations

The minor-axis and polar radii of gyration are

\[
r_y=\sqrt{\frac{I_y}{A}},
\qquad
r_0=\sqrt{\frac{I_x+I_y}{A}+x_0^2},
\]

where \(y_0=0\) by symmetry.

The uncoupled flexural buckling loads are

\[
N_{cr,x}=\frac{\pi^2EI_x}{L_{ex}^2},
\qquad
N_{cr,y}=\frac{\pi^2EI_y}{L_{ey}^2}.
\]

The uncoupled torsional reference load is

\[
N_{cr,T}
=
\frac{1}{r_0^2}
\left(
GJ+\frac{\pi^2EI_w}{L_{ez}^2}
\right).
\]

For a channel symmetric about the \(x\)-axis, define

\[
q=\left(\frac{x_0}{r_0}\right)^2,
\qquad
\beta=1-q.
\]

The lower torsional-flexural eigenvalue is

\[
N_{cr,TF}
=
\frac{
N_{cr,y}+N_{cr,T}
-
\sqrt{
\left(N_{cr,y}+N_{cr,T}\right)^2
-4\beta N_{cr,y}N_{cr,T}
}
}{2\beta}.
\]

The common flexural coefficient is

\[
\frac{\pi^2E}{L^2}
=
\frac{\pi^2(210000)}{3000^2}
=
0.230290769\ \mathrm{N/mm^4}.
\]

## Candidate screening

Loads below are in kN.

| Section | \(A\) (mm²) | \(r_y\) (mm) | \(r_0\) (mm) | \(\beta\) | \(N_{cr,x}\) | \(N_{cr,y}\) | \(N_{cr,T}\) | \(N_{cr,TF}\) |
|:---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| VM-C140 | 620 | 30.586 | 76.450 | 0.698185 | 449.067 | 133.569 | 103.434 | 74.756 |
| VM-C160 | 800 | 33.967 | 86.918 | 0.682187 | 736.930 | 212.558 | 173.000 | 121.490 |
| VM-C180 | 1080 | 38.730 | 98.058 | 0.680810 | 1255.085 | 373.071 | 345.144 | 228.986 |
| VM-C200 | 1350 | 42.199 | 108.161 | 0.671420 | 1888.384 | 553.619 | 592.179 | 363.591 |

For every section, the torsional-flexural load is the lowest elastic critical load.

Using curve b, \(\alpha=0.34\),

\[
\bar{\lambda}=\sqrt{\frac{Af_y}{N_{cr}}},
\]

\[
\Phi=\frac12\left[1+\alpha(\bar{\lambda}-0.2)+\bar{\lambda}^2\right],
\]

\[
\chi=
\min\left[
1,\,
\frac{1}{\Phi+\sqrt{\Phi^2-\bar{\lambda}^2}}
\right].
\]

Since \(L_{ez}=3.0\ \mathrm{m}>2.50\ \mathrm{m}\),

\[
k_{VM}=0.92,
\qquad
N_{b,Rd}=0.92\,\chi Af_y.
\]

| Section | \(Af_y\) (kN) | Governing \(N_{cr}\) (kN) | \(\bar{\lambda}\) | \(\Phi\) | \(\chi\) | \(N_{b,Rd}\) (kN) | \(N_{Ed}/N_{b,Rd}\) | Check |
|:---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|:---|
| VM-C140 | 220.100 | 74.756 | 1.7159 | 2.2298 | 0.26864 | 54.398 | 2.114 | Fails slenderness and resistance |
| VM-C160 | 284.000 | 121.490 | 1.5289 | 1.8947 | 0.33180 | 86.693 | 1.327 | Fails slenderness and resistance |
| VM-C180 | 383.400 | 228.986 | 1.2940 | 1.5231 | 0.42980 | 151.603 | 0.7586 | Passes |
| VM-C200 | 479.250 | 363.591 | 1.1481 | 1.3202 | 0.50708 | 223.578 | 0.5144 | Passes, but heavier |

## Detailed check of the lightest passing section: VM-C180

### 1. Radii of gyration

\[
r_y=\sqrt{\frac{1.620\times10^6}{1080}}
=\sqrt{1500}
=38.7298\ \mathrm{mm}.
\]

\[
r_0^2
=
\frac{(5.450+1.620)\times10^6}{1080}+55.4^2
\]

\[
=6546.2963+3069.1600
=9615.4563\ \mathrm{mm^2},
\]

\[
r_0=98.0584\ \mathrm{mm}.
\]

### 2. Flexural buckling

\[
N_{cr,x}
=
\frac{\pi^2(210000)(5.450\times10^6)}{3000^2}
=
1255.085\ \mathrm{kN}.
\]

\[
N_{cr,y}
=
\frac{\pi^2(210000)(1.620\times10^6)}{3000^2}
=
373.071\ \mathrm{kN}.
\]

### 3. Torsional reference load

\[
GJ=(81000)(2590)
=209.790\times10^6\ \mathrm{N\,mm^2},
\]

\[
\frac{\pi^2EI_w}{L_{ez}^2}
=
\frac{\pi^2(210000)(13.50\times10^9)}{3000^2}
=
3108.925\times10^6\ \mathrm{N\,mm^2}.
\]

Therefore,

\[
N_{cr,T}
=
\frac{(209.790+3108.925)\times10^6}{9615.4563}
=
345.144\ \mathrm{kN}.
\]

### 4. Torsional-flexural buckling

\[
\beta
=
1-\frac{55.4^2}{9615.4563}
=
1-0.319190
=
0.680810.
\]

\[
N_{cr,TF}
=
\frac{
373.071+345.144
-
\sqrt{(373.071+345.144)^2
-4(0.680810)(373.071)(345.144)}
}{2(0.680810)}
\]

\[
=
\frac{718.2149-406.4231}{1.3616195}
=
228.986\ \mathrm{kN}.
\]

Thus,

\[
N_{cr}=\min(1255.085,\ 373.071,\ 228.986)
=228.986\ \mathrm{kN}.
\]

### 5. Slenderness and reduction factor

\[
Af_y=(1080)(355)=383400\ \mathrm{N}=383.400\ \mathrm{kN}.
\]

\[
\bar{\lambda}
=
\sqrt{\frac{383.400}{228.986}}
=
\sqrt{1.674338}
=
1.293962.
\]

The maker limit is satisfied:

\[
1.293962<1.30.
\]

For curve b:

\[
\Phi
=
\frac12\left[
1+0.34(1.293962-0.2)+1.293962^2
\right]
=
1.523143,
\]

\[
\chi
=
\frac{1}{
1.523143+
\sqrt{1.523143^2-1.293962^2}
}
=
0.429802.
\]

### 6. Design resistance and utilization

\[
N_{b,Rd}
=
0.92(0.429802)(1080)(355)
=
151603\ \mathrm{N}
=
151.603\ \mathrm{kN}.
\]

\[
\text{Utilization}
=
\frac{115}{151.603}
=
0.7586
=
75.86\%.
\]

## Final conclusion

The lightest satisfactory section is **VM-C180**. Its governing mode is **torsional-flexural buckling**. It satisfies both the maker slenderness limit, \(1.29396<1.30\), and the factored load requirement, \(151.603>115\ \mathrm{kN}\). VM-C140 and VM-C160 fail, while VM-C200 passes but is heavier.
